newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta consumer spending eases but still high.
newsitem.headline: Malta consumer spending eases but still high.

text.p: The growth rate of private consumer spending slowed in the first nine months of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995, although it was still high, a review of the Maltese economy shows.
Maltese households were also spending more of their disposable income.
The recently-released government review says consumer expenditure between January and September reached 592.9 million Maltese pounds ($1.6 billion), up by 65.1 million pounds, or 12.3 percent.
In the first nine months of 1995 expenditure had risen by 16.3 per cent.

The largest advances were on food, drinks, clothing, recreation and travel, apparently indicating that the Maltese economy was closely following consumption patterns and buying behaviour of more developed economies, the survey says.
Household disposable income rose by 4.5 percent to 644.5 million pounds, with private consumption taking 92 percent of it in the period reviewed compared to 88.1 percent in the previous period.

The survey said that in this context, the dangers of domestic inflationary pressures should be highlighted and that if the decline in the savings ratio was sustained, investment activity may be curtailed. This could result in the pace of economic activity slowing, the survey said.
